Baseline looks more tractable: it mostly means blocking privileged mode, host namespaces, hostPath, host ports, extra capabilities, and unconfined seccomp. I'm weighing whether to offer a target-profile option and how to handle the risky fixes, whether as a safe subset or with explicit warnings.

I'm settling on how to word the answer in French: a short explanation that the Pod Security profiles map onto the existing catalog, plus one question on risk appetite and one on how the profile gets chosen. Trivy's KSV checks probably line up with those profiles, but I haven't confirmed which profile each one belongs to, so I'll flag that as unverified.

input.message:
## Corrections automatiques pour les profils Pod Security : possible en partie

**Ce qui existe déjà.** DevDesk a un catalogue de correctifs pour les manifestes Kubernetes (`internal/remediation/k8s.go`, `docs/architecture/scanning.md`, §3.80). Trois règles, et seulement sur un manifeste brut (un chart Helm ou un overlay Kustomize est refusé) :
- `KSV-0017` : `privileged: true` devient `false` ;
- `KSV-0001` : `allowPrivilegeEscalation` devient `false`, ou la ligne est insérée si elle est absente ;
- `K8S-API-REMOVED` : l'`apiVersion` est renommée, seulement pour les types sans autre changement.

Le correctif est une édition d'octets : commentaires, ancres et fins de ligne survivent. Une confirmation montre le diff exact. Le fichier est ensuite re-scanné pour savoir si la règle a disparu.

**Ce qui a été écarté exprès, et c'est le cœur de ta question.** Le profil `restricted` exige justement ce que DevDesk refuse de corriger seul : `runAsNonRoot`, `readOnlyRootFilesystem`, retirer toutes les capabilities (`drop: [ALL]`), un profil seccomp. La raison notée : ces correctifs passent la règle mais peuvent empêcher le conteneur de démarrer. Les limites de ressources n'ont pas de valeur universelle, et seccomp peut se placer au niveau du pod ou du conteneur. De plus, `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false` est refusé par l'API Kubernetes sur un conteneur privilégié ou avec `CAP_SYS_ADMIN`.

**Sur les trois profils**
- `privileged` : aucune restriction, donc rien à corriger.
- `baseline` : il interdit surtout les conteneurs privilégiés, le réseau et les PID de l'hôte, `hostPath`, les ports d'hôte, les capabilities dangereuses et un seccomp `Unconfined`. Une partie est corrigeable sans risque pour le démarrage (un booléen à `false`), d'autres non (retirer un `hostPath`).
- `restricted` : il cumule `baseline` et les règles ci-dessus. C'est le plus risqué à corriger automatiquement.

**Pas encore vérifié :** si DevDesk sait à quel profil appartient chaque `KSV-*` de Trivy. La sélection « conforme au profil X » en dépend.

  ## Faisabilité : conformité PSS (baseline / restricted) avec Trivy seul
  
  **Verdict : c'est faisable, sous conditions.** Trivy 0.76.2 indique bien le profil de chaque check. En revanche, sur 20 contrôles Pod Security, seuls 4 groupes ont un correctif qui ne peut pas empêcher le démarrage : privileged, allowPrivilegeEscalation, les trois espaces de noms hôte, et seccomp quand il est absent. Les deux premiers existent déjà. Pour tout le reste, DevDesk décrit ce qui manque sans écrire. Effort total : M à L, en 6 étapes livrables. Je n'ai modifié aucun fichier du dépôt ; mes manifestes de test sont sous `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-anthoni-projects-workspace-entire-anthnel-devdesk/18dbe3ec-6b73-4a6a-a3cc-91d7baf58f89/scratchpad/` (m1, m2, m3).
  
  ### Questions bloquantes
  
  1. **Que filtre le réglage ?**
     - (a) Seulement les checks Pod Security : sous baseline, les findings restricted-only sont masqués, et les autres KSV restent visibles (KSV-0014 readOnlyRootFilesystem, limites de ressources, RBAC…).
     - (b) Tous les KSV hors profil.
     - **Recommandation : (a).** Avec (b), un profil baseline ferait disparaître des findings de sécurité réels.
  2. **Valeur par défaut et ensemble des valeurs.**
     - (a) `all | baseline | restricted`, avec `all` par défaut : c'est le comportement actuel et rien ne change pour les contextes existants.
     - (b) `baseline | restricted` seulement.
     - **Recommandation : (a).** Remarque : `restricted` ne masque rien, puisqu'il contient baseline. Il ne change que le cadrage (« manque pour restricted »).
  3. **Masquer ou marquer ?** On peut retirer les findings hors profil, ou les garder visibles avec une colonne ou étiquette `PSS` et un filtre. **Recommandation : marquer.** Masquer un finding dans un outil de sécurité nourrit un faux sentiment de conformité.
  4. **hostNetwork / hostPID / hostIPC à `false`.** Le conteneur démarre, mais l'édition peut casser le fonctionnement d'agents de nœud (CNI, exporters, ingress sur l'hôte) : c'est un choix explicite de l'auteur que l'on inverse.
     - (a) Proposer partout, le diff de confirmation le disant.
     - (b) Décliner sur les DaemonSet.
     - **Recommandation : (a), avec la phrase dans la confirmation.**
  5. **KSV-0104 sous baseline.** Trivy le déclenche aussi quand seccomp est **absent**, alors que la norme PSS baseline n'interdit que `Unconfined` explicite (vérifié sur m2).
     - (a) L'afficher et proposer RuntimeDefault (plus strict que la norme).
     - (b) Sous baseline, ne garder KSV-0104 que sur un `Unconfined` explicite.

## Corrections par profil Pod Security : faisable, effort M à L en 6 étapes

Vérifié par l'`architect` avec Trivy 0.76.2 (bundle de checks local), sur de petits manifestes d'essai (Pod, Deployment, CronJob, multi-documents). Rien n'a été modifié dans le dépôt. Le brief est dans `docs/product/pss-profile-fixes/brief.md`.

**Trivy sait à quel profil appartient chaque check**, mais de façon imparfaite :
- Chaque check porte un lien vers la norme avec une ancre `#baseline` ou `#restricted`. DevDesk jette aujourd'hui cette information : `TrivyMisconfiguration` ne décode pas `References`.
- Les specs de conformité de Trivy (`k8s-pss-baseline-0.1`) **omettent KSV-0009 et KSV-0010** (hostNetwork et hostPID). Les reprendre sous-déclarerait ces contrôles.
- **Recommandation de l'architect :** une table de ~20 entrées maintenue à la main, indexée par identifiant de règle, avec un test sur une sortie Trivy enregistrée pour détecter les écarts.

**Parmi les 20 contrôles Pod Security, seuls 4 groupes ont un correctif sûr :**
- `privileged` et `allowPrivilegeEscalation` : existent déjà ;
- `hostNetwork`, `hostPID`, `hostIPC` à `false` (KSV-0008/9/10) : nouveau, effort S ;
- seccomp `RuntimeDefault` quand il est absent partout (KSV-0104 et KSV-0030) : nouveau, effort M, vérifié sur un CronJob.

Pour tout le reste, DevDesk décrit ce qui manque, sans écrire : `runAsNonRoot`, `drop ALL`, `hostPath`, `hostPort`, SELinux, types de volume, etc.

**Plan en 6 étapes livrables seules :** table KSV → profil (S), réglage `scan.pss_profile` (S), onglet Misconfigurations avec étiquette et filtre (M), correctif hostNetwork/PID/IPC (S), correctif seccomp (M), textes « ce qui manque » pour ~14 règles (M). « Rendre le fichier conforme en un seul diff » est un L, reporté.

**Risques**
- **Faux sentiment de conformité :** zéro finding Trivy ne veut pas dire « admis par Pod Security Admission ». Trivy dévie de la norme : KSV-0104 et KSV-0022 sont plus stricts, et il ne lit que les types de workload qu'il connaît. Le libellé doit dire « aucune violation détectée par Trivy pour baseline », jamais « conforme ».
- **seccomp `RuntimeDefault` :** une charge qui tournait en `Unconfined` et appelle des syscalls bloqués (outils de debug, `unshare`, `mount`) ne le montre qu'à l'exécution. Le re-scan ne le voit pas.
- **Faits non vérifiés :** les refus de validation de l'API Kubernetes pour un pod Windows (seccomp, hostNetwork exigé par HostProcess).

options.description: Les findings hors profil restent visibles avec une étiquette PSS et un filtre. Valeurs `all`, `baseline`, `restricted`, défaut `all` : rien ne change pour les contextes existants. Seuls les checks Pod Security sont concernés, jamais les autres KSV.

options.label: Masquer les findings hors profil
options.description: Sous `baseline`, les findings propres à restricted disparaissent. L'architect le déconseille : un outil de sécurité qui masque nourrit un faux sentiment de conformité.

questions.question: hostNetwork / hostPID / hostIPC à `false` : le conteneur démarre, mais ça peut casser des agents de nœud (CNI, exporters, ingress sur l'hôte). On fait quoi ?

options.label: Proposer partout, avec avertissement (Recommandé)
options.description: Le diff de confirmation dit que cela inverse un choix explicite de l'auteur. Rien n'est jamais écrit sans confirmation.

options.label: Décliner sur les DaemonSet
options.description: Pas de proposition de correction sur un DaemonSet, où ces valeurs sont presque toujours voulues. DevDesk dit seulement ce qui manque.

questions.question: KSV-0104 sous `baseline` : Trivy le déclenche aussi quand seccomp est absent, alors que la norme baseline n'interdit que `Unconfined` explicite. Que fait DevDesk ?

options.label: Garder seulement `Unconfined` explicite (Recommandé)
options.description: Sous baseline, DevDesk ne retient KSV-0104 que sur un `Unconfined` explicite, pour ne pas contredire le profil annoncé. Sous restricted, seccomp absent reste signalé (KSV-0030) et corrigeable.

options.label: Afficher et proposer RuntimeDefault quand même
options.description: Plus strict que la norme. Simple à implémenter, mais l'outil signale sous baseline ce que baseline n'exige pas.

Mode autonome (pas de discussion), dépôt /home/anthoni/projects/workspace-entire/anthnel/devdesk. Charge la skill `product-team:user-stories`. N'écris RIEN dans Plane. Écris docs/product/pss-profile-fixes/stories.md (checkout principal, non commité, en français) et mets à jour brief.md (section Décisions + faisabilité + questions ouvertes tranchées). Lis docs/product/pss-profile-fixes/brief.md et docs/product/g-exact-search/stories.md (format).

Faisabilité (architect, 2026-11-22, faits vérifiés avec Trivy 0.76.2 sauf mention) :
- Trivy donne le profil via l'ancre `#baseline`/`#restricted` du lien PSS dans `References` de chaque check ; DevDesk jette `References` aujourd'hui (`internal/scan/trivy.go`, `TrivyMisconfiguration`). Les specs de conformité de Trivy omettent KSV-0009 et KSV-0010. Recommandation retenue : table maintenue à la main (~20 entrées) indexée par `RuleKey` dans `internal/remediation`, avec un test sur une sortie Trivy enregistrée ; un finding avec une ancre PSS absente de la table est étiqueté « profil d'après Trivy, sans correctif ».
- 4 groupes de correctifs sûrs : privileged (KSV-0017) et allowPrivilegeEscalation (KSV-0001) existent déjà ; NOUVEAUX : hostIPC/hostNetwork/hostPID → false (KSV-0008/0009/0010, effort S) ; seccompProfile RuntimeDefault au niveau pod quand absent partout (KSV-0104 baseline, KSV-0030 restricted, effort M ; refus si un conteneur ou le pod met Unconfined/Localhost, annotations seccomp présentes, pod Windows, securityContext en ligne, pod spec partagé par alias YAML ; chemin du pod spec : Pod `spec`, Deployment/StatefulSet/DaemonSet/ReplicaSet/Job `spec.template.spec`, CronJob `spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec`).
- Sans correctif sûr, DevDesk dit ce qui manque pour le profil, dans le refus grisé existant : KSV-0103, 0022, 0023, 0024, 0002, 0025/0026/0027, 0028, 0012, 0105, 0106 (≈14 règles).
- Réglage `scan.pss_profile` (config, nouveau champ sans migration, modèle `base_image_track`), valeurs `all | baseline | restricted`, étiquette PSS + filtre dans l'onglet Misconfigurations et l'en-tête, projection `pss_profile` dans le MCP `scan_result`.
- Effort : étapes 1 table (S), 2 réglage (S), 3 onglet (M), 4 correctif host* (S), 5 correctif seccomp (M), 6 textes « ce qui manque » (M) ; « rendre le fichier conforme en un seul diff » = L, reporté.
- Risques à écrire : libellé « aucune violation détectée par Trivy pour <profil> », jamais « conforme » (Trivy dévie : KSV-0104 et KSV-0022 plus stricts que la norme, ne lit que les types connus) ; seccomp RuntimeDefault peut casser à l'exécution une charge qui tournait en Unconfined (le re-scan ne le voit pas) ; hostNetwork à false peut casser des agents de nœud ; faits non vérifiés : refus de validation de l'API pour un pod Windows (seccomp, hostNetwork requis par HostProcess).

DÉCISIONS DE L'UTILISATEUR (validées 2026-11-22) : (1) le réglage MARQUE et FILTRE (étiquette PSS + filtre), il ne masque rien ; valeurs `all | baseline | restricted`, défaut `all` (aucun changement pour les contextes existants) ; il ne concerne que les checks Pod Security, jamais les autres KSV. (2) hostNetwork/hostPID/hostIPC → false proposé PARTOUT, y compris DaemonSet, avec un avertissement dans le diff de confirmation (« cela inverse un choix explicite de l'auteur ; peut casser des agents de nœud »), jamais écrit sans confirmation. (3) Sous `baseline`, KSV-0104 n'est retenu que sur un `Unconfined` explicite (seccomp absent n'est signalé que sous `restricted`, KSV-0030) ; KSV-0022 : le dire dans le texte sans filtrer. Hypothèses que tu reprends de l'architect, à marquer « Hypothèse: à valider » : une correction par finding (comme aujourd'hui), le « rendre conforme en lot » est Won't pour ce jalon ; le réglage est par contexte (YAML) et modifiable depuis la vue de configuration ; correctifs appliqués aussi aux conteneurs init/éphémères quand le pod spec est concerné.

Découpe INVEST (par valeur visible, jamais par couche technique) : propose 4 stories : S-01 voir le profil PSS de chaque finding et régler le profil cible (table + réglage + étiquette/filtre + en-tête ; Must) ; S-02 corriger hostNetwork/hostPID/hostIPC (Must ou Should) ; S-03 corriger seccomp absent (Should) ; S-04 voir précisément ce qui manque pour le profil quand aucune correction sûre n'existe (Must ou Should). Chacune : critères Given/When/Then testables (3 à 7), hors périmètre, hypothèses, questions ouvertes, effort S/M/L (reprend l'architect), priorité MoSCoW, dépendances. Ajoute une section « Won't / plus tard » (lot « rendre conforme », Helm/Kustomize, corrections risquées). Compte rendu court : stories, efforts, hypothèses à valider, questions ouvertes.

content.text:
Le `pm` rédige les stories avec tes trois décisions de l'`architect` :
- le réglage `scan.pss_profile` **marque et filtre**, sans rien masquer, avec les valeurs `all | baseline | restricted` et `all` par défaut ;
- `hostNetwork`, `hostPID` et `hostIPC` à `false` sont proposés partout, DaemonSet compris, avec un avertissement dans le diff ;
- sous `baseline`, seccomp n'est retenu que s'il est explicitement `Unconfined`.

Le découpage est prévu en 4 stories, qui apportent chacune une valeur visible :
1. Voir le profil PSS de chaque finding et régler le profil cible.
2. Corriger `hostNetwork`, `hostPID` et `hostIPC`.
3. Corriger seccomp quand il est absent.
4. Voir précisément ce qui manque quand aucune correction sûre n'existe.

Le « rendre le fichier conforme en un seul diff » est placé en « plus tard ».

L'utilisateur a validé explicitement (2026-11-22) les 4 stories de docs/product/pss-profile-fixes/stories.md, leurs hypothèses de comportement (filtre désactivé à l'ouverture, étiquette visible sous `all`, avertissement host* pour les trois champs et tous types, avertissement seccomp) et la création dans Plane.

3. Si l'outil le permet, ajoute une relation « bloquée par » de S-04 vers S-01 (workitem_relation) ; sinon la mention dans la description suffit.
4. Ajoute les identifiants (DEVDESK-NNN) à stories.md (S-01 à S-04) et mets à jour la ligne de statut. Ne touche à rien d'autre ; ne commite pas.

# Brief — kyverno-policies

Plane : DEVDESK-10 (`[§3.85] Kyverno : appliquer les politiques de l'organisation aux manifestes Kubernetes`, Backlog, critères « À définir »). Le titre Plane dit « de l'organisation » ; depuis la décision du 2026-11-22 (ci-dessous), le premier objectif est le jeu standard de Kyverno ; à renommer sur demande, rien n'a été modifié.
Source : `docs/backlog.md` §3.85 (première moitié ; la seconde, ce que kube-linter aurait vu, est DEVDESK-11 et reste hors de ce brief).

## Idée

DevDesk applique des politiques Kyverno aux manifestes Kubernetes d'un dépôt scanné, pour faire respecter des règles que Trivy et kubeconform ne connaissent peut-être pas. **Premier objectif (2026-11-22) : vérifier en strict avec les jeux de politiques standard fournis par Kyverno** (dépôt `kyverno/policies`, profil `restricted` des Pod Security Standards). Les politiques propres à une organisation viennent après, dans une étape ultérieure.

## Problème

§3.80 a écarté Kyverno pour ne pas multiplier les outils : `kyverno apply` n'embarque aucune politique, ce n'est donc pas un catalogue de plus. Aujourd'hui, DevDesk scanne les manifestes avec Trivy (sécurité, dont des contrôles `KSV-*` proches des Pod Security Standards) et kubeconform (validité de schéma). Le jeu standard `restricted` de Kyverno recoupe vraisemblablement une grande partie de ces `KSV-*` : la question n'est plus « l'organisation a-t-elle des règles que personne n'applique », mais « le jeu standard strict voit-il des violations que Trivy ne voit pas déjà ». Si la réponse est non, l'étage n'apporte rien et c'est un résultat acceptable.

## Décisions (validées avec l'utilisateur)

- Source des politiques : **un répertoire local** (réglage envisagé `scan.kyverno_policies`). L'étage ne tourne que s'il est renseigné. Pas de dépôt git ni d'URL dans ce jalon.
- **Provenance (précisée le 2026-11-22)** : l'utilisateur **clone lui-même** `kyverno/policies` dans un répertoire et renseigne `scan.kyverno_policies` ; DevDesk ne livre ni ne télécharge rien (non-objectif maintenu).
- **Premier objectif (2026-11-22)** : le jeu standard de Kyverno en strict. « Strict » = profil **`restricted`** des PSS, au-dessus de `baseline`. Les politiques d'organisation viennent après (S7 de `stories.md`).
- Affichage : les violations sont des findings de la catégorie **Misconfiguration**, onglet Misconfigurations existant, colonne Source `kyverno` (même décision que pour kubeconform, §3.80).
- Gravité : celle de la politique (annotation `policies.kyverno.io/severity`) ; **Medium** par défaut si elle est absente.
- Périmètre : **jalon 1 = manifestes bruts** (ceux que `k8s.Discover` trouve) ; **jalon 2 = rendu Helm et Kustomize**, partagé avec l'étage `k8s-schema` plutôt que refait.
- Les règles `mutate` ne servent pas de correctif (elles réécrivent la ressource entière, réserve de §3.78).

## Le jeu standard visé (constat web du 2026-11-22, non remesuré)

À reconfirmer sur le clone par le critère 1 de S0 ; sources : `https://github.com/kyverno/policies`, `https://kyverno.io/docs/guides/pod-security/`.

- Sur `main`, le dossier est `pod-security-vpol/` (sous-dossiers `baseline/` et `restricted/`, plus `EXCEPTIONS.md`). L'ancien chemin `pod-security/restricted` renvoie une 404 sur `main`.
- `restricted/` : 7 politiques (`disallow-capabilities-strict`, `disallow-privilege-escalation`, `disallow-proc-mount-strict`, `require-run-as-non-root-user`, `require-run-as-nonroot`, `restrict-seccomp-strict`, `restrict-volume-types`). `baseline/` : 12 d'après son `kustomization.yaml` (nombre à vérifier). Le profil `restricted` des PSS incluant `baseline`, le jeu strict est de l'ordre de **19 politiques (à vérifier)**.
- **Variante CEL** : `main` ne livre que du CEL en `policies.kyverno.io/v1` (`ValidatingPolicy`, `validationActions: [Audit]`, gravité par annotation, `minversion` 1.19.1 sur la politique lue).
- **Variante héritée `ClusterPolicy`** : le README de `main` dit que les exemples `ClusterPolicy`, `Policy` et leurs équivalents de nettoyage ont été retirés. La documentation et le site de Kyverno mentionnent encore des chemins `pod-security` et `pod-security-cel` ; quel ref du dépôt porte encore la variante héritée n'est pas établi (aucune release affichée) : à vérifier. La contradiction de Kyverno 1.20 sur les `ClusterPolicy` (rejet ou simple avertissement) devient donc une question de compatibilité de version et de cluster plus ancien, plus un risque pour l'utilisateur tant qu'il utilise `main`.
- Les politiques lues utilisent une variable CEL `exceptions.allowedImages` ; son évaluation par le CLI hors cluster est à mesurer.

## Points à vérifier (faisabilité)

- Un rapport Kyverno (`--policy-report --output-format json`) donne-t-il un numéro de ligne ? Sinon, comment le retrouver (pointeur de ressource → ligne, comme `internal/k8s` le fait pour kubeconform) ?
- Le mode d'exécution de l'outil (`auto | binary | image`) et son entrée dans la table des outils (`internal/scan/toolbox.go`, §3.86) : quelle catégorie, quelle dépendance, quel signalement s'il est absent.
- Comportement sur politique invalide, aucun manifeste, politique de type `generate` ou `verifyImages` (peu probable dans le jeu `restricted`, mais pas exclu).

## Risques identifiés par la critique

Hypothèses à tester d'abord (le spike S0 de `stories.md` les mesure) :

- **A'. Valeur au-delà de Trivy (remplace l'ancienne hypothèse A, « l'utilisateur a un jeu d'organisation non appliqué ailleurs »).** Le jeu standard `restricted` apporte des violations que Trivy (`KSV-*` et ses contrôles Pod Security) ne voit pas déjà. **C'est LE critère de valeur et le risque principal de no-go** : le profil `restricted` recoupe fortement les `KSV-*`. Mesure : mêmes manifestes, mêmes ressources, taux de recouvrement O et valeur résiduelle (seuils T1 et T2 de S0). Un no-go « Trivy voit déjà l'essentiel » est un résultat acceptable.
- **B. Verdict fiable hors cluster.** Les politiques donnent un verdict fiable sans cluster. Le risque est plus faible qu'avec un jeu d'organisation (les politiques lues ne semblent pas utiliser `apiCall`, `configMap`, `request.*`), mais la variable `exceptions` n'est pas testée.
- **C. Rattachement sans ambiguïté.** Une violation se rattache à un fichier et une ligne (base + overlays Kustomize, rendu Helm), alors que le rapport ne porte que des références d'objet.

Autres points relevés :

- Version : le jeu `main` annonce une version minimale de Kyverno 1.19.1 ; Kyverno 1.20 n'exécuterait plus les `ClusterPolicy` d'après la documentation (le code et la doc se contredisent, à mesurer) ; le backlog §3.85 cite 1.19.1. Une newsletter dit 1.20.0 étiquetée le 12 novembre, sans note de version officielle trouvée.
- Format JSON du rapport non vérifié : champs `severity`, `rule`, `resources`, `message` ; un document JSON par rapport. Si toutes les politiques du jeu portent la même gravité, la règle « gravité de la politique » ne différencie rien.
- Politique invalide et répertoire vide : codes de sortie et messages inconnus ; risque de faux vert.
- Gravité `Audit` / `Enforce` ignorée ; valeurs de `policies.kyverno.io/severity` divergentes selon les sources.
- Doublons avec les `KSV-*` de Trivy : désormais le sujet central, plus un détail.
- Règles autogen : les politiques CEL lues listent explicitement `Deployment`, `CronJob`, etc. ; à confirmer.
- Version du CLI à aligner avec celle du cluster.

## Décision : spike d'abord (2026-11-22, précisée le même jour)

L'utilisateur a décidé de **faire d'abord un spike de mesure** avant toute story d'implémentation : une demi-journée (à valider), livrable `docs/measurements/<date>-kyverno-apply.md`, qui se termine par une décision **go / no-go / pivot (Trivy + contrôles Rego)** selon des seuils validés avant le run. **Précision :** le spike mesure le jeu standard `restricted` de `kyverno/policies`, cloné par l'utilisateur, et non plus un jeu d'organisation ; le recouvrement avec Trivy est le critère de valeur, et un no-go motivé par ce recouvrement est un résultat acceptable. Détail, critères et seuils révisés : story S0 de `stories.md`. Les stories d'implémentation (jalons 1 et 2, gravité, doublons, politiques d'organisation) ne sont écrites qu'après un go ; leurs pistes sont listées en fin de `stories.md`. Entrées à fournir par l'utilisateur : où cloner et quel ref, la version du CLI à mesurer, les dépôts de test, qui lance les commandes et sur quelle machine. Il n'a plus de jeu de politiques à fournir.

## Non-objectifs

- Pas de téléchargement de politiques (git, URL) par DevDesk, pas de catalogue livré avec DevDesk : l'utilisateur clone lui-même (maintenu).
- Pas, dans ce jalon, de politiques propres à l'organisation : étape ultérieure (S7).
- Pas de correctif automatique à partir de `mutate`.
- Pas de contrôles croisés entre objets ni de sondes liveness/readiness (DEVDESK-11).
- Pas de client de cluster : DevDesk lit des fichiers.

# Stories — g-exact-search

## Epic : Recherche du prompt `g`

### S-01 — Basculer entre recherche floue et exacte dans le prompt g
Epic : Recherche du prompt `g` — Priorité : Must — Effort : S — Plane : DEVDESK-678

moitié de l'effort.)

# Brief — g-exact-search

## Idée

Dans le prompt `g` de `ws` et de `ge` (forge explorer), pouvoir basculer entre la
recherche floue (comportement actuel) et une recherche exacte.

## Problème

Le prompt `g` (`internal/ui/fuzzy`, partagé par `ws` et `ge`) n'a qu'un scorer,
`fuzzy.Match` : une requête est acceptée si ses lettres apparaissent dans l'ordre dans le
chemin, même dispersées. `dev` remonte donc aussi tout chemin contenant d, e, v dans
l'ordre. Quand on connaît le nom cherché, ces faux positifs noient le bon résultat.

## Décisions (validées avec l'utilisateur)

- « Exact » = sous-chaîne contiguë, insensible à la casse.
- Bascule par une touche dans le prompt : `tab` (libre dans le finder, sans conflit avec
  la saisie ; `ctrl+e` écarté, c'est « fin de ligne » dans le champ).
- Exception déclarée à la Rule 135 (`.claude/rules/tui-forms.md`, surface `fuzzy/finder`) :
  la bascule utilise `tab` (décision validée par l'utilisateur après la faisabilité). `tab`
  doit figurer dans l'en-tête des raccourcis et dans l'aide de la vue, avec la description
  du mode vers lequel il bascule (« Exact match » / « Fuzzy match »).
- Mode affiché dans la barre `Find`.
- Un seul réglage commun à `ws` et `ge`, non mémorisé : chaque ouverture de `g` démarre en
  `fuzzy`.
- Classement en `exact` : un match en début de chemin ou juste après `/` passe devant, puis
  le chemin le plus court.
- Parcours allégé : pas de recherche ni de critique (besoin clair, impact limité à un
  composant partagé).

## MVP

- Touche `tab` : `fuzzy` ↔ `exact`, la liste se recalcule immédiatement.
- Libellé du mode actif dans la barre `Find`.
- Seuil minimum de caractères et compteur de correspondances inchangés.

## Non-objectifs

- Pas de mémorisation (ni session, ni YAML).
- Pas de sensibilité à la casse, de regex, ni de correspondance sur un segment entier.
- Pas de réglage par vue.
- Pas de changement du scorer flou existant.

## Métriques de succès

- Dans `ws` et `ge`, `tab` bascule le mode et recalcule la liste.
- En `exact`, `dev` ne retourne que des chemins contenant littéralement « dev » ; `wsd` ne
  retourne rien.
- En `fuzzy`, aucun changement observable.

## Points techniques repérés

- `internal/ui/fuzzy/match.go` (`Match`) et `finder.go` (`rematch`, `RenderBar`,
  `Update`) concentrent le changement.
- Docs à mettre à jour : `docs/architecture/workspaces.md`, `forge.md`.

À utiliser avant une feature non triviale pour concevoir la solution, comparer des options, définir composants, interfaces et données, et produire un plan d'implémentation en étapes ; ou pour évaluer rapidement la faisabilité et l'effort d'un brief ou de stories. - dev-team:debugger: Débogueur. À utiliser face à un bug, une erreur, une stack trace, un test qui échoue ou un comportement inattendu dont la cause n'est pas évidente. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write, Bash, Skill, mcp__plugin_dev-team_context7)

- dev-team:reviewer: Relecteur de code. À utiliser après toute modification de code pour détecter bugs, régressions, écarts avec les critères d'acceptation et les conventions du projet. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Skill, ToolSearch, mcp__plane-reviewer)

- dev-team:security-reviewer: Auditeur sécurité. À utiliser sur un diff ou un composant touchant authentification, autorisations, données sensibles, entrées externes, dépendances, secrets ou infrastructure. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Skill, WebSearch, WebFetch)

- dev-team:tester: Testeur, en TDD. À utiliser pour écrire les tests d'une étape avant son implémentation (tests qui échouent), ou pour la vérification finale : suite complète et couverture des critères d'acceptation. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write, Bash, Skill, ToolSearch, mcp__plane-tester)

Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. - general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

## Reference

    locate  ->  entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "..."
    impact  ->  entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X   (one shot: callers, callees, type consumers, data flow, co-change, siblings)
    callers ->  entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol X --relation CALLS --direction in
    change  ->  entire graph diff --base A --head B --json
    detect  ->  entire graph capabilities --json   (inventory-only languages have no relations)
    stats   ->  entire graph stats --repo .        (human-facing token-savings report; not part of your workflow — do not run it unless asked)

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP; a Proxy row says whether a proxy variable applies, the checks themselves stay direct, DEVDESK-582) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only) + a path trace under Diagnostics (Trace Path button, or `H` on the route row; no separate tab since DEVDESK-471) (native path trace, on native Linux, native Windows (IPv4 only, ICMP echoes through `iphlpapi`, DEVDESK-486) and WSL2: on macOS and WSL1 the button, `H`, `enter` and `ctrl+o` are greyed and the footer says why, DEVDESK-334; the column starts with this machine, its interface and its gateway; `ctrl+o` can start it from a running Docker Engine container instead (container and network rows, hops still traced from this machine); `H` on the Diagnostics route row opens the trace level on that host without starting it (greyed with the reason on an unsupported platform or a target the trace refuses; its interface and gateway rows reuse the Local route check's reading of the same address, read once, DEVDESK-473), and in the trace level `enter` starts or restarts it, `ctrl+o` picks the source, `esc` cancels then goes back where it came from; under WSL2 the source row says `WSL2 (VM), not the Windows host` with the networking mode, and in NAT mode the gateway and TTL 1 hop are tagged `Windows host (virtual switch)` only when proven, DEVDESK-333; the interface row says `no route` when the kernel proves there is none and `undetermined` when the routing table could not be read, a no-route error keeps the local rows, a trace that ends on the hop limit or the deadline folds its silent tail into one `silent` row and marks the `last to answer` hop, and the target refuses a `:port`, DEVDESK-335)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
mise run ci           # the five checks in order (fmt-check, vet, lint, build, test-race), stops at the first failure; unlike check it rewrites no file and also runs build and test-race. `test-race` is the only test run (`-race` covers `go test`); `mise run test` stays available alone for the fast local loop. CI runs fmt-check, vet, lint and build in the `Lint and build` job and `test-race` in the `Test` job, on every pull request, docs-only ones included (the docs-only shortcut applies to `Lint and build` only); the whole CI targets under 10 minutes, so run this locally before a PR to catch a red check early

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Nexus tests replay recorded fixtures (DEVDESK-511, DEVDESK-580).** Three campaigns
in `internal/nexusfixture/fixtures/` (`catalog`, `cachedonly`, `access`) replay through
`fakenexus`: `mise run test` needs no bench, cluster or secret. A `record: pending` file is never
versioned (`TestNoPendingFixtureIsVersioned`); `DEVDESK_FIXTURE_RECORDING=1` only in a local recording session.
`nexus-bench record` without `--state` applies no state filter and can overwrite an `upstream-cut` fixture.
Bench writes go only through `nexus-bench:*` tasks and the guarded `DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH_SCENARIOS=1` test.
Dated measures live in `docs/measurements/`; a measure contradicting a criterion or the code is frozen and noted, never fixed in the same PR.

**Scanner containers and the proxy (DEVDESK-583, D164).** Every `run --rm` a scanner
issues goes through `containerRun{…}.cmd()` (`internal/scan/container_run.go`): the proxy
variables travel as `-e NAME` with the value in the child environment, never in argv. The
guard `TestContainerGuard*` (`internal/netproxy/container_guard_test.go`) fails on any other
`"run"` literal; only the two permanent exceptions in that file are allowed. The tests of
`internal/scan`, `internal/app` and `internal/ui/security` neutralise the seams
`proxyForward` / `containerForward` in their `TestMain`, so a developer's `HTTPS_PROXY` does not
change an exact argv. The `TestMain` of `internal/app`
also replaces `detectTools` (`internal/app/scan_tools.go`, production value `scan.Detect`) with an
empty report, so `App.Init` never runs the `trivy`, `gitleaks` and `plumber` of the machine
(DEVDESK-645); `TestInitDoesNotRunTheScannersOfTheHost` and `TestDetectToolsIsScanDetectInProduction`
guard it.

**Tests and the host secret store (DEVDESK-610).** By default `credentials.Select` and
`KeyringAvailable` reach the real keyring of the machine (Secret Service over D-Bus on
Linux); a locked keyring blocks the whole suite until the timeout. A test binary that can
reach them isolates the store: `fakekeyring.Install()` in `TestMain`, then
`fakekeyring.Fresh(t)` (or `FreshUnreachable(t, err)` for a locked keyring) per test, from
`internal/testutil/fakekeyring`. `isolateHome(t)` already calls `Fresh` in `internal/app` and
`internal/ui/setup`. Two guards enforce it: at run time, any keyring or `git credential` call
in a test binary without the fake panics with `DEVDESK-610` and the operation; statically,
`TestHostStoreGuard*` (`internal/credentials/hoststore_guard_test.go`) fails on K1 (go-keyring
imported outside `internal/credentials`), K2 (`SwapHostStoreForTest` in non-test code) and K3
(`fakekeyring` imported by non-test code). The seam is `credentials.HostStore` and
`SwapHostStoreForTest`, reserved for tests (it panics outside a test binary). Limits: the
runtime guard only sees the paths a test runs; the static one misses an aliased package
name, a dynamic import and an external binary; `gitHelperUsable` reads the git config
unguarded; `Install` and `Fresh` are global, so no `t.Parallel`. See
`docs/architecture/configuration.md`, "Testing code that reaches the secret store".

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

- `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing` - ICMP ping functionality (maintained fork of go-ping/ping)
- `github.com/google/go-github/v68` - GitHub API client (§3.6)
- `github.com/libp2p/go-netroute` - which interface a destination leaves by, on all three platforms (§3.44)
- `golang.org/x/sys` - direct (Rule 303): the socket calls of `internal/nettrace` (`IP_TTL`, `IP_RECVERR`, `recvmsg` on the error queue); `x/sys/windows` serves `iphlpapi` (the Windows path trace, `IcmpSendEcho2`)
- `github.com/zalando/go-keyring` - host secret manager (wincred / Keychain / Secret Service), no cgo
- `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` - YAML configuration

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Views render through `Render()`** (Bubble Tea v2): a top-level view implements
`Render() string` and `View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.Render()) }`; only the
router (`App.View()`) sets terminal state such as `AltScreen` and `BackgroundColor`. Components keep
`View() string`. Colours are `color.Color`; hex literals stay in `theme/colors.go`.

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

# TUI — Rule index

TUI rules are split across 5 topic files:

| File | Rules | Content |
|---------|--------|---------|
| [`tui-layout.md`](tui-layout.md) | 101, 107, 108, 111, 112, 123, 124, 130, 134, 137, 138 | General layout, keybindings, viewport, tabs, shortcuts header, format descriptions, shortcuts obviousness |
| [`tui-theme.md`](tui-theme.md) | 102, 105, 115, 117, 118, 119, 127, 129 | Colors, lipgloss background, `theme.*` helpers, language |
| [`tui-forms.md`](tui-forms.md) | 103, 104, 113, 114, 120, 121, 131, 132, 133, 135, 140 | Forms, modals, focus, status icons, value cycling, WrappedInput, key assignment, invalid field |
| [`tui-tables.md`](tui-tables.md) | 106, 116, 122, 125, 136, 139 | Tables, column widths, plain-text cells + color via `Style`, filter bar, body never replaced (loading or message) |
| [`tui-behavior.md`](tui-behavior.md) | 109, 110, 126, 128 | Bubble Tea (Cmd/Update), scan cache, footer messages (three levels, one component) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer, never in the body: with the shared activity dot (`Status.Activity`, `●`/`○`, `SetBlinkPhase`), for a view's own load as well as for work the router tracks. The braille spinner API is removed (DEVDESK-377): nothing under `internal/` imports `bubbles/v2/spinner` or names `Status.Spinner`, `SetSpinnerFrame`, `theme.SpinnerMessage` or `theme.SpinnerStyle` (`TestNoViewImportsTheBubblesSpinner`, `TestRemovedSpinnerSymbolsStayGone`), with no exception. A new `Activity` value not driven by the jobs registry must implement `WantsBlink()`, or the dot stays fixed.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a loading screen or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 140** — An invalid form field is underlined through `theme.StyleInvalidField` (the only entry point to the underline API), and the error is also in the footer at level Error, derived on every render. The underline is never the only carrier.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

# Planning Rules

## Implementation Plans

- **Location**: Always write implementation plans to `.claude/plans/` in the current project directory.
- **Format**: Use Markdown format for plans.
- **Naming**: Use descriptive names like `feature-name-plan.md` or `YYYY-MM-DD-feature-name.md`.

## Antigravity IDE Integration

When using the Antigravity IDE extension:
- Save all implementation plans to `.claude/plans/` relative to the project root.
- Create the directory if it doesn't exist before saving plans.
- Plans should be accessible from both Claude Code CLI and Antigravity IDE.

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X

7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP; a Proxy row says whether a proxy variable applies, the checks themselves stay direct, DEVDESK-582) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only) + a path trace under Diagnostics (Trace Path button, or `H` on the route row; no separate tab since DEVDESK-471) (native path trace, on native Linux, native Windows (IPv4 only, ICMP echoes through `iphlpapi`, DEVDESK-486) and WSL2: on macOS and WSL1 the button, `H`, `enter` and `ctrl+o` are greyed and the footer says why, DEVDESK-334; the column starts with this machine, its interface and its gateway; `ctrl+o` can start it from a running Docker Engine container instead (container and network rows, hops still traced from this machine); `H` on the Diagnostics route row opens the trace level on that host without starting it (greyed with the reason on an unsupported platform or a target the trace refuses; its interface and gateway rows reuse the Local route check's reading of the same address, read once, DEVDESK-473), and in the trace level `enter` starts or restarts it, `ctrl+o` picks the source, `esc` cancels then goes back where it came from; under WSL2 the source row says `WSL2 (VM), not the Windows host` with the networking mode, and in NAT mode the gateway and TTL 1 hop are tagged `Windows host (virtual switch)` only when proven, DEVDESK-333; the interface row says `no route` when the kernel proves there is none and `undetermined` when the routing table could not be read, a no-route error keeps the local rows, a trace that ends on the hop limit or the deadline folds its silent tail into one `silent` row and marks the `last to answer` hop, and the target refuses a `:port`, DEVDESK-335)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
mise run ci           # the five checks in order (fmt-check, vet, lint, build, test-race), stops at the first failure; unlike check it rewrites no file and also runs build and test-race. `test-race` is the only test run (`-race` covers `go test`); `mise run test` stays available alone for the fast local loop. CI runs fmt-check, vet, lint and build in the `Lint and build` job and `test-race` in the `Test` job, on every pull request, docs-only ones included (the docs-only shortcut applies to `Lint and build` only); the whole CI targets under 10 minutes, so run this locally before a PR to catch a red check early

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Nexus tests replay recorded fixtures (DEVDESK-511, DEVDESK-580).** Three campaigns
in `internal/nexusfixture/fixtures/` (`catalog`, `cachedonly`, `access`) replay through
`fakenexus`: `mise run test` needs no bench, cluster or secret. A `record: pending` file is never
versioned (`TestNoPendingFixtureIsVersioned`); `DEVDESK_FIXTURE_RECORDING=1` only in a local recording session.
`nexus-bench record` without `--state` applies no state filter and can overwrite an `upstream-cut` fixture.
Bench writes go only through `nexus-bench:*` tasks and the guarded `DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH_SCENARIOS=1` test.
Dated measures live in `docs/measurements/`; a measure contradicting a criterion or the code is frozen and noted, never fixed in the same PR.

**Scanner containers and the proxy (DEVDESK-583, D164).** Every `run --rm` a scanner
issues goes through `containerRun{…}.cmd()` (`internal/scan/container_run.go`): the proxy
variables travel as `-e NAME` with the value in the child environment, never in argv. The
guard `TestContainerGuard*` (`internal/netproxy/container_guard_test.go`) fails on any other
`"run"` literal; only the two permanent exceptions in that file are allowed. The tests of
`internal/scan`, `internal/app` and `internal/ui/security` neutralise the seams
`proxyForward` / `containerForward` in their `TestMain`, so a developer's `HTTPS_PROXY` does not
change an exact argv. The `TestMain` of `internal/app`
also replaces `detectTools` (`internal/app/scan_tools.go`, production value `scan.Detect`) with an
empty report, so `App.Init` never runs the `trivy`, `gitleaks` and `plumber` of the machine
(DEVDESK-645); `TestInitDoesNotRunTheScannersOfTheHost` and `TestDetectToolsIsScanDetectInProduction`
guard it.

**Tests and the host secret store (DEVDESK-610).** By default `credentials.Select` and
`KeyringAvailable` reach the real keyring of the machine (Secret Service over D-Bus on
Linux); a locked keyring blocks the whole suite until the timeout. A test binary that can
reach them isolates the store: `fakekeyring.Install()` in `TestMain`, then
`fakekeyring.Fresh(t)` (or `FreshUnreachable(t, err)` for a locked keyring) per test, from
`internal/testutil/fakekeyring`. `isolateHome(t)` already calls `Fresh` in `internal/app` and
`internal/ui/setup`. Two guards enforce it: at run time, any keyring or `git credential` call
in a test binary without the fake panics with `DEVDESK-610` and the operation; statically,
`TestHostStoreGuard*` (`internal/credentials/hoststore_guard_test.go`) fails on K1 (go-keyring
imported outside `internal/credentials`), K2 (`SwapHostStoreForTest` in non-test code) and K3
(`fakekeyring` imported by non-test code). The seam is `credentials.HostStore` and
`SwapHostStoreForTest`, reserved for tests (it panics outside a test binary). Limits: the
runtime guard only sees the paths a test runs; the static one misses an aliased package
name, a dynamic import and an external binary; `gitHelperUsable` reads the git config
unguarded; `Install` and `Fresh` are global, so no `t.Parallel`. See
`docs/architecture/configuration.md`, "Testing code that reaches the secret store".

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

## Dependencies

Go 1.27 (`go 1.27.3` in `go.mod`). Key libraries (versions as in `go.mod`):
- `charm.land/bubbletea/v2` (v2.1.1) - TUI framework (v2: `tea.KeyPressMsg`, `tea.PasteMsg`, `View() tea.View`)
- `charm.land/bubbles/v2` (v2.2.1) - Pre-built TUI components (table, textinput, viewport)
- `charm.land/lipgloss/v2` (v2.0.6) - Styling (no global colour profile; colours are `image/color.Color`)
- `github.com/charmbracelet/colorprofile` (v0.4.3) - colour profile `main.go` forces under Windows Terminal (replaces `termenv`)
- `github.com/NimbleMarkets/ntcharts/v2` (v2.9.0) - dashboard sparkline
- `github.com/charmbracelet/x/ansi` - ANSI-safe width, strip and cut
- `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go` - GitLab API client
- `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing` - ICMP ping functionality (maintained fork of go-ping/ping)
- `github.com/google/go-github/v68` - GitHub API client (§3.6)
- `github.com/libp2p/go-netroute` - which interface a destination leaves by, on all three platforms (§3.44)
- `golang.org/x/sys` - direct (Rule 303): the socket calls of `internal/nettrace` (`IP_TTL`, `IP_RECVERR`, `recvmsg` on the error queue); `x/sys/windows` serves `iphlpapi` (the Windows path trace, `IcmpSendEcho2`)
- `github.com/zalando/go-keyring` - host secret manager (wincred / Keychain / Secret Service), no cgo
- `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` - YAML configuration

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Views render through `Render()`** (Bubble Tea v2): a top-level view implements
`Render() string` and `View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.Render()) }`; only the
router (`App.View()`) sets terminal state such as `AltScreen` and `BackgroundColor`. Components keep
`View() string`. Colours are `color.Color`; hex literals stay in `theme/colors.go`.

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

# TUI — Rule index

TUI rules are split across 5 topic files:

| File | Rules | Content |
|---------|--------|---------|
| [`tui-layout.md`](tui-layout.md) | 101, 107, 108, 111, 112, 123, 124, 130, 134, 137, 138 | General layout, keybindings, viewport, tabs, shortcuts header, format descriptions, shortcuts obviousness |
| [`tui-theme.md`](tui-theme.md) | 102, 105, 115, 117, 118, 119, 127, 129 | Colors, lipgloss background, `theme.*` helpers, language |
| [`tui-forms.md`](tui-forms.md) | 103, 104, 113, 114, 120, 121, 131, 132, 133, 135, 140 | Forms, modals, focus, status icons, value cycling, WrappedInput, key assignment, invalid field |
| [`tui-tables.md`](tui-tables.md) | 106, 116, 122, 125, 136, 139 | Tables, column widths, plain-text cells + color via `Style`, filter bar, body never replaced (loading or message) |
| [`tui-behavior.md`](tui-behavior.md) | 109, 110, 126, 128 | Bubble Tea (Cmd/Update), scan cache, footer messages (three levels, one component) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer, never in the body: with the shared activity dot (`Status.Activity`, `●`/`○`, `SetBlinkPhase`), for a view's own load as well as for work the router tracks. The braille spinner API is removed (DEVDESK-377): nothing under `internal/` imports `bubbles/v2/spinner` or names `Status.Spinner`, `SetSpinnerFrame`, `theme.SpinnerMessage` or `theme.SpinnerStyle` (`TestNoViewImportsTheBubblesSpinner`, `TestRemovedSpinnerSymbolsStayGone`), with no exception. A new `Activity` value not driven by the jobs registry must implement `WantsBlink()`, or the dot stays fixed.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a loading screen or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 140** — An invalid form field is underlined through `theme.StyleInvalidField` (the only entry point to the underline API), and the error is also in the footer at level Error, derived on every render. The underline is never the only carrier.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.
